nodes.name: Metaphysics
nodes.description: The branch of philosophy investigating the fundamental nature of reality, being, and existence.

nodes.name: Epistemology
nodes.description: The branch of philosophy studying the nature, sources, and limits of knowledge and justified belief.

nodes.name: Ethics
nodes.description: The branch of philosophy that systematizes, defends, and recommends concepts of right and wrong conduct.

nodes.name: Aesthetics
nodes.description: The philosophical study of beauty, taste, art, and aesthetic experience.

nodes.name: Philosophical Logic
nodes.description: The philosophical study of logic, its foundations, and its application to philosophical problems.

nodes.name: Political Philosophy
nodes.description: The normative study of government, justice, rights, liberty, and political authority.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Mind
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature of the mind, mental events, consciousness, and their relation to the body.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Language
nodes.description: The philosophical study of meaning, reference, truth, and the relationship between language and reality.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Science
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the assumptions, methods, and implications of the sciences.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Religion
nodes.description: The philosophical examination of religious concepts, beliefs, arguments, and practices.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Mathematics
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature, foundations, and ontology of mathematical objects and truth.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Law
nodes.description: The philosophical analysis of law, legal systems, and legal reasoning.

nodes.name: Social Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical study of social structures, collective life, and social institutions.

nodes.name: History of Philosophy
nodes.description: The historical study of philosophical traditions, schools, and arguments across cultures.

nodes.name: Philosophy of History
nodes.description: The philosophical study of historical knowledge, meaning, and the structure of historical narratives.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Technology
nodes.description: The philosophical study of technology, its nature, and its effects on human life and values.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Education
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the aims, methods, and value of education.

nodes.name: Ontology
nodes.description: The philosophical study of being, existence, and the categories of what there is.

nodes.name: Mereology
nodes.description: The philosophical study of parts, wholes, and the relations between them.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Time
nodes.description: The philosophical investigation of the nature of time, temporal passage, and change.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Space
nodes.description: The philosophical investigation of the nature of space and spatial relations.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Causation
nodes.description: The philosophical analysis of cause, effect, and causal explanation.

nodes.name: Modality
nodes.description: The philosophical study of necessity, possibility, and possible worlds.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Identity
nodes.description: The philosophical study of identity, sameness, and persistence over time.

nodes.name: Free Will and Determinism
nodes.description: The philosophical debate over whether agents possess free will and how it relates to causation.

nodes.name: Abstract Objects
nodes.description: The philosophical study of non-spatiotemporal entities such as numbers, properties, and propositions.

nodes.name: Mind-Body Problem
nodes.description: The philosophical problem of how mental states relate to physical states of the body.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Perception
nodes.description: The philosophical study of how perceptual experience yields knowledge of the world.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Memory
nodes.description: The philosophical study of memory as a source and store of knowledge.

nodes.name: Social Epistemology
nodes.description: The study of knowledge as a collective achievement involving groups and institutions.

nodes.name: Formal Epistemology
nodes.description: The use of formal methods from logic and probability theory to model knowledge and belief.

nodes.name: Epistemology of Testimony
nodes.description: The philosophical study of knowledge and justification acquired from the words of others.

nodes.name: Skepticism
nodes.description: The philosophical position that questions the possibility of knowledge or justified belief.

nodes.name: Virtue Epistemology
nodes.description: The approach to epistemology centered on intellectual virtues and cognitive character.

nodes.name: Metaethics
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature, semantics, and metaphysics of moral judgments.

nodes.name: Normative Ethics
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the standards by which actions are judged right or wrong.

nodes.name: Applied Ethics
nodes.description: The application of ethical theory to concrete practical problems in life and professions.

nodes.name: Moral Psychology
nodes.description: The empirical and philosophical study of moral judgment, motivation, and character.

nodes.name: Deontology
nodes.description: The ethical theory that the rightness of actions depends on duties and rules rather than consequences.

nodes.name: Consequentialism
nodes.description: The ethical theory that the rightness of actions depends solely on their outcomes or consequences.

nodes.name: Virtue Ethics
nodes.description: The ethical tradition centered on the cultivation of virtuous character rather than rules or results.

nodes.name: Ethics of Care
nodes.description: An ethical framework emphasizing interpersonal relationships, empathy, and responsibility of care.

nodes.name: Contractualism
nodes.description: The ethical theory that grounds morality in principles that rational parties would agree to.

nodes.name: Utilitarianism
nodes.description: The consequentialist theory that actions are right insofar as they maximize overall well-being.

nodes.name: Bioethics
nodes.description: The ethical study of issues arising from biology, medicine, and the life sciences.

nodes.name: Medical Ethics
nodes.description: The ethics of clinical practice, patient care, and the duties of medical professionals.

nodes.name: Business Ethics
nodes.description: The application of ethical principles to commerce, corporate conduct, and economic activity.

nodes.name: Environmental Ethics
nodes.description: The ethical study of human obligations toward the natural environment and non-human beings.

nodes.name: Animal Ethics
nodes.description: The ethical study of the moral status and treatment of non-human animals.

nodes.name: Technology Ethics
nodes.description: The ethical study of the design, use, and social impact of technologies.

nodes.name: Military Ethics
nodes.description: The ethics of warfare, including just war theory and the conduct of combatants.

nodes.name: Research Ethics
nodes.description: The ethical standards governing the responsible conduct of scientific and scholarly research.

nodes.name: AI Ethics
nodes.description: The ethical study of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and their societal consequences.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Art
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature, definition, and value of art.

nodes.name: Ontology of Art
nodes.description: The philosophical study of what kind of thing an artwork is and how it exists.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Music
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature, value, and experience of music.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Literature
nodes.description: The philosophical study of literary works, interpretation, and literary value.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Film
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature, interpretation, and value of cinema.

nodes.name: Aesthetic Experience
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the character and value of experiences of beauty and art.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Beauty
nodes.description: The philosophical study of beauty, the sublime, and aesthetic value.

nodes.name: Modal Logic
nodes.description: The study of logic enriched with operators for necessity and possibility.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Truth
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature and theories of truth.

nodes.name: Theories of Justice
nodes.description: Philosophical accounts of what justice requires in the distribution of benefits and burdens.

nodes.name: Social Contract Theory
nodes.description: The theory that legitimate political authority derives from an implicit agreement among people.

nodes.name: Liberalism
nodes.description: The political philosophy centered on individual liberty, equality, and limited government.

nodes.name: Libertarianism
nodes.description: The political philosophy emphasizing maximal individual freedom and minimal state coercion.

nodes.name: Communitarianism
nodes.description: The political philosophy stressing the role of community and social context in shaping values.

nodes.name: Republicanism
nodes.description: The political tradition centered on civic virtue, the common good, and freedom from domination.

nodes.name: Socialism
nodes.description: The political philosophy advocating collective or public ownership and egalitarian distribution.

nodes.name: Marxism
nodes.description: The political and economic philosophy founded on the analysis of class, capital, and historical materialism.

nodes.name: Anarchism
nodes.description: The political philosophy that rejects hierarchical authority and advocates self-governed association.

nodes.name: Feminist Philosophy
nodes.description: Philosophy that critically examines gender, power, and the assumptions of the philosophical tradition.

nodes.name: Egalitarianism
nodes.description: The view that people should be treated as moral equals in the distribution of goods and standing.

nodes.name: Distributive Justice
nodes.description: The philosophical study of how society should fairly allocate resources, wealth, and opportunity.

nodes.name: Consciousness
nodes.description: The philosophical study of phenomenal awareness and subjective experience.

nodes.name: Qualia
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the subjective, qualitative character of conscious experience.

nodes.name: Intentionality
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the aboutness or directedness of mental states toward objects.

nodes.name: Mental Causation
nodes.description: The philosophical problem of how mental states can cause physical events.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Emotion
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature, rationality, and role of emotions.

nodes.name: Personal Identity
nodes.description: The philosophical study of what makes a person the same over time.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Cognitive Science
nodes.description: The philosophical examination of the concepts and methods of cognitive science.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Meaning
nodes.description: The philosophical study of linguistic meaning and semantics.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Reference
nodes.description: The philosophical study of how words pick out objects in the world.

nodes.name: Speech Act Theory
nodes.description: The theory that utterances perform actions such as promising, asserting, and commanding.

nodes.name: Pragmatics
nodes.description: The philosophical study of meaning in context and how speakers use language to communicate.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Physics
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the concepts and foundations of physical theories.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Biology
nodes.description: The philosophical study of biological concepts such as evolution, function, and species.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Social Science
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the methods, explanations, and objectivity of the social sciences.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Medicine
nodes.description: The philosophical study of health, disease, and the epistemology of medicine.

nodes.name: Philosophical Theology
nodes.description: The use of philosophical methods to articulate and defend theological doctrines.

nodes.name: Natural Theology
nodes.description: The attempt to establish truths about God through reason and observation of the natural world.

nodes.name: Problem of Evil
nodes.description: The philosophical problem of reconciling the existence of evil with an all-powerful, all-good God.

nodes.name: Religious Epistemology
nodes.description: The philosophical study of whether and how religious belief can be rationally justified.

nodes.name: Foundations of Mathematics
nodes.description: The study of the logical and set-theoretic foundations on which mathematics rests.

nodes.name: Mathematical Platonism
nodes.description: The view that mathematical objects exist independently of human thought.

nodes.name: Mathematical Nominalism
nodes.description: The view that mathematical objects do not exist as abstract entities.

nodes.name: Natural Law Theory
nodes.description: The theory that law derives its authority from universal moral principles discoverable by reason.

nodes.name: Legal Positivism
nodes.description: The theory that law is a social construction independent of its moral merits.

nodes.name: Critical Theory
nodes.description: The interdisciplinary social theory originating in the Frankfurt School that critiques domination and ideology.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Race
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the concepts, ontology, and ethics of race and racism.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Gender
nodes.description: The philosophical study of gender, sex, and their social construction.

nodes.name: Social Ontology
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the nature of social entities such as groups, institutions, and norms.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Culture
nodes.description: The philosophical study of culture, cultural meaning, and cultural difference.

nodes.name: Speculative Philosophy of History
nodes.description: The attempt to discern large-scale patterns, meaning, and direction in the course of history.

nodes.name: Analytic Philosophy of History
nodes.description: The philosophical analysis of historical knowledge, explanation, and narrative.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence
nodes.description: The philosophical study of machine intelligence, mind, and the possibility of thinking machines.

nodes.name: Western Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical tradition originating in ancient Greece and developing through Europe and beyond.

nodes.name: Chinese Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical traditions of China spanning Confucian, Daoist, and Buddhist schools.

nodes.name: Indian Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical traditions of the Indian subcontinent including Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain schools.

nodes.name: Islamic Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical tradition of the Islamic world, especially falsafa and kalam.

nodes.name: Japanese Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical traditions of Japan, including Buddhist and modern schools.

nodes.name: Korean Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical traditions of Korea, blending Confucianism, Buddhism, and indigenous thought.

nodes.name: African Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical traditions and contemporary debates arising from African cultures and thought.

nodes.name: Latin American Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical traditions of Latin America, including liberation and decolonial thought.

nodes.name: Ancient Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophy of Greco-Roman antiquity from the Presocratics through late antiquity.

nodes.name: Medieval Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophy of the Middle Ages, developed largely within Christian, Jewish, and Islamic traditions.

nodes.name: Renaissance Philosophy
nodes.description: The revival of classical learning and humanism in early modern Europe.

nodes.name: Modern Philosophy
nodes.description: Early modern philosophy from Descartes through the Enlightenment.

nodes.name: German Idealism
nodes.description: The idealist philosophical movement of Kant, Fichte, Schelling, and Hegel.

nodes.name: Analytic Philosophy
nodes.description: The twentieth-century tradition emphasizing logical clarity, argument, and language.

nodes.name: Continental Philosophy
nodes.description: The nineteenth- and twentieth-century European traditions including phenomenology and existentialism.

nodes.name: Pragmatism
nodes.description: The American philosophical tradition that ties meaning and truth to practical consequences.

nodes.name: Process Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical tradition holding that becoming and process are fundamental to reality.

nodes.name: Presocratic Philosophy
nodes.description: The early Greek philosophy before Socrates concerned with cosmology and first principles.

nodes.name: Platonism
nodes.description: The philosophy of Plato and its successors, centered on the theory of Forms.

nodes.name: Aristotelianism
nodes.description: The philosophy of Aristotle and its tradition, emphasizing empirical inquiry and virtue.

nodes.name: Hellenistic Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophy of the Hellenistic and Roman periods focused on ethics and the good life.

nodes.name: Stoicism
nodes.description: The Hellenistic school teaching virtue, reason, and acceptance of what lies beyond our control.

nodes.name: Epicureanism
nodes.description: The ancient school teaching that pleasure and freedom from fear constitute the good life.

nodes.name: Pyrrhonian Skepticism
nodes.description: The ancient skeptical school that suspends judgment to achieve tranquility.

nodes.name: Cynicism
nodes.description: The ancient school advocating a life of virtue in accord with nature and free of convention.

nodes.name: Neoplatonism
nodes.description: The late-antique philosophical system elaborating Plato through emanation and the One.

nodes.name: Scholasticism
nodes.description: The medieval school method that used dialectical reasoning to reconcile faith and reason.

nodes.name: Patristic Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophy of the early Church Fathers synthesizing Christian doctrine with Greek thought.

nodes.name: Rationalism
nodes.description: The epistemological view that reason is the primary source of knowledge.

nodes.name: Empiricism
nodes.description: The epistemological view that experience and the senses are the primary source of knowledge.

nodes.name: Enlightenment Philosophy
nodes.description: The eighteenth-century movement championing reason, liberty, and progress.

nodes.name: Logical Positivism
nodes.description: The early twentieth-century movement holding that only verifiable statements are meaningful.

nodes.name: Ordinary Language Philosophy
nodes.description: The mid-century movement analyzing philosophical problems through everyday linguistic usage.

nodes.name: Phenomenology
nodes.description: The philosophical study of the structures of experience and consciousness as lived.

nodes.name: Existentialism
nodes.description: The philosophical movement centered on freedom, authenticity, and the meaning of existence.

nodes.name: Hermeneutics
nodes.description: The theory and methodology of interpretation, especially of texts and meaning.

nodes.name: Poststructuralism
nodes.description: The late twentieth-century movement critiquing stable structures of meaning, knowledge, and power.

nodes.name: Deconstruction
nodes.description: The critical practice of uncovering the instabilities and oppositions within texts and concepts.

nodes.name: Confucianism
nodes.description: The ethical and political tradition of Confucius emphasizing virtue, ritual, and social harmony.

nodes.name: Daoism
nodes.description: The philosophical tradition of Laozi and Zhuangzi centered on the Way and naturalness.

nodes.name: Legalism
nodes.description: The ancient Chinese school advocating strict law, state power, and administrative control.

nodes.name: Mohism
nodes.description: The ancient Chinese school of Mozi advocating universal love and utility.

nodes.name: School of Names
nodes.description: The ancient Chinese school devoted to logic, language, and the analysis of names.

nodes.name: Yin-Yang School
nodes.description: The ancient Chinese cosmological school explaining change through yin and yang and five phases.

nodes.name: Neo-Confucianism
nodes.description: The Song and Ming dynasty revival of Confucianism synthesizing metaphysics and ethics.

nodes.name: Chinese Buddhist Philosophy
nodes.description: The Buddhist philosophical schools of China, including Tiantai, Huayan, and Chan.

nodes.name: Hindu Philosophy
nodes.description: The orthodox philosophical schools of the Hindu tradition.

nodes.name: Buddhist Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical analysis of mind, reality, and liberation within Buddhist traditions.

nodes.name: Jain Philosophy
nodes.description: The philosophical tradition of Jainism centered on non-violence and pluralism of viewpoints.

nodes.name: Carvaka
nodes.description: The ancient Indian materialist school denying the soul and afterlife.

nodes.name: Samkhya
nodes.description: The dualist Hindu school enumerating the principles of consciousness and matter.

nodes.name: Yoga Philosophy
nodes.description: The Hindu school systematizing meditation and discipline as the path to liberation.

nodes.name: Nyaya
nodes.description: The Hindu school of logic and epistemology analyzing valid inference and knowledge.

nodes.name: Vaisesika
nodes.description: The Hindu atomistic school categorizing the fundamental kinds of existents.

nodes.name: Mimamsa
nodes.description: The Hindu school of Vedic exegesis and the philosophy of ritual and language.

nodes.name: Vedanta
nodes.description: The Hindu tradition interpreting the Upanishads and the nature of ultimate reality.

nodes.name: Advaita Vedanta
nodes.description: The non-dualist Vedanta school teaching the identity of self and ultimate reality.

nodes.name: Dvaita Vedanta
nodes.description: The dualist Vedanta school distinguishing the individual soul from God.

nodes.name: Madhyamaka
nodes.description: The Mahayana school of the Middle Way analyzing the emptiness of all phenomena.

nodes.name: Yogacara
nodes.description: The Mahayana school of mind-only philosophy analyzing consciousness and perception.

nodes.name: Falsafa
nodes.description: The Islamic philosophical tradition drawing on Greek thought to analyze reason and reality.

nodes.name: Kalam
nodes.description: The Islamic speculative theology that uses rational argument to defend doctrine.

nodes.name: Illuminationism
nodes.description: The mystical philosophical system of Suhrawardi centered on light and illumination.

nodes.name: Kyoto School
nodes.description: The twentieth-century Japanese school synthesizing Zen Buddhism and Western philosophy.

nodes.name: Ubuntu Philosophy
nodes.description: The southern African ethic of shared humanity, communality, and relational personhood.

nodes.name: Philosophy of Liberation
nodes.description: The Latin American movement philosophizing from the perspective of the oppressed and colonized.
